constraints_found.constraint: Mina is vegetarian (strict diet, deal-breaker); she needs several real meat-free curries, not a side
source_lines: liam: fine. but this time mina gets a full meal like the rest of us. no plate of fries
liam: burger day in spring. i had a double stack. she had fries, because nothing else on the menu worked for her
maya: oh, like pizza day when she offered to pick the pepperoni off. absolutely not
mina: ...okay. somewhere with a few curries i can actually order would be really nice if you don't mind

venue_reasoning.downtown_tamarind_lane: Curry, $, review 1 shows three meat-free curries as full plates, review 2 shows very fast counter service. Meets everything.
venue_reasoning.downtown_copper_pot: Curry, $, fast, but every pot is meat and only plain rice for the non-meat eater. Fails Mina's diet (deal-breaker).
venue_reasoning.downtown_cardamom_house: Curry, fast, good veg options, but $$ and the review calls it a treat-yourself lunch. One tier over budget, so -1 star (2 stars).
venue_reasoning.downtown_indigo_arch: Curry, $, veg options, but slow service; the reviewer was late back to the office. Misses the quick lunch (2 stars).
venue_reasoning.downtown_pepper_tree: Fast, $, good veggie burger, but it's burgers, not curry. Misses the craving and echoes the burger-day story (2 stars).

notes: Mina's vegetarianism is never stated outright. You have to work it out from the fries and pepperoni stories plus 'a few curries i can actually order'. That's a good layered clue and still fair, since both stories point the same way, and every review mentions someone who 'doesn't eat meat' or 'skips meat', which confirms the reading.
The budget is implied ('if it's pricey', 'what a whole lunch should' cost) and never given as a tier. Reading it as $ seemed obvious, and only Cardamom House is $$, so it works.

Each decoy fails on exactly one constraint, so it's a clean one-answer puzzle. Moderately easy once the diet clue is decoded. It could be tough for players who miss the fries and pepperoni stories, because Copper Pot's meat-only menu only shows in its review.
Pepper Tree's veggie burger review is a nice twist: it fixes the fries problem from burger day but is still the wrong cuisine.
